newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill would require state to take over aid.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill would require state to take over aid.

text.p: A California state Senator has introduced a bill that would require the state to take over general assistance programs from counties, his office said on Monday.
Senator Mike Thompson's measure would change general assistance from a 100 percent county-funded program to a statewide program. Counties would pay only a share of the costs, Thompson's office said.
General assistance is a cash grant program for indigent adults with no dependents. It provides aid for those who have no other resources. The average grant is $217 per month.

Thompson, a Democrat, said his proposal was prompted by federal welfare reform and by Republican Gov. Pete Wilson's recent budget proposal, which would relieve counties of their general assistance mandate without proposing a back-up funding source.
"Our goal is to provide relief to cash-strapped local governments while preventing California's social safety net from becoming a disjointed checkerboard," the senator said.
Under the measure, general assistance would become a statewide program. Counties would be relieved of at least 30 percent of their current costs.

Thompson's legislation will be heard in the Senate Health and Human Services Committee in early March. From there, it will most likely be referred to a special conference committee on welfare reform, which will be co-chaired by Thompson.
